R1114.note: Bounds check correctly moved to segment.size(); claimedCapacity param left unused rather than removed per contract's third clause, but this is disclosed and changes no observable behavior.

R1115.note: Adds can:update,order matching the sibling PUT/POST routes' established authorization pattern; consistent, no observable side effects.

R1116.note: Closes the timing side-channel with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare but still compares raw plaintext passwords - the code's own comment flags storage as 'always unhashed,' the more fundamental CWE-287 defense (hash+verify) is not addressed.

R1117.note: DOMPurify.sanitize before bypassSecurityTrustHtml is the correct pattern and preserves allowed formatting; cited CVE-2026-41238 for DOMPurify could not be verified.

R1118.note: Eliminating the shell/process call closes the injection vector, but the fixed code writes the literal text "echo " + param to the response instead of just param (what the real OS echo would output), a silent output change the write-up incorrectly claims is behavior-preserving.

R1119.note: Pins JWKS fetch to a trusted, server-configured URL instead of the token's own jku header; still returns ClaimsPrincipal/throws via the same ValidateToken call, matching the stated contract.

R1120.note: Removes the erroneous double URL-decode and adds toRealPath()+startsWith() containment, closing both the decode-based and generic traversal vectors without altering legitimate-file behavior.

R1121.note: Swapping to fast-xml-parser removes XXE capability entirely (processEntities:false is largely redundant since the library never resolves external entities), but fast-xml-parser's default numeric auto-coercion can silently turn orderId from a string into a number in the JSON response, which the write-up does not disclose.

R1122.note: Standard PreparedStatement with bound parameter; same query semantics and result set.

R1123.note: json_encode() correctly escapes for the JS string-literal context (including forward slashes, closing the </script> breakout) and preserves the value for legitimate note text.

R1124.note: The strnlen()-based NUL-termination check on the source buffer is the actual fix and is sound; the added %255s field width is not itself sufficient (255 > the 64-byte source) so its stated rationale is off, but it does not undermine the real fix and is harmless.

R1125.note: html/template auto-escapes Author/Excerpt; the escaping is the intended and disclosed behavior change, nothing else altered.

R1126.note: Correctly identifies that ArgumentList alone is insufficient for a .bat target and makes the allowlist regex the load-bearing defense; restriction to alnum/hyphen/underscore is disclosed and consistent with a report-name identifier.

R1127.note: doc.XmlResolver = null is the standard XmlDocument XXE mitigation; does not affect parsing of documents without external references.

R1128.note: Allowlist plus path.resolve()+startsWith() containment closes traversal; appending '.js' matches the file's own documented plugin layout ('./plugins/*.js'), so no legitimate use is broken.

R1129.note: EL expression ${displayName} cannot see the scriptlet-local Java variable `displayName` (never published via setAttribute), so <c:out> would render an empty string instead of the actual name - silently breaks the welcome-message feature while the write-up presents it as working.

R1130.note: Only checks scheme is http/https, so redirects to any attacker-controlled external host (e.g. https://evil.com) still succeed - the primary CWE-601 vector remains open - while it now rejects legitimate scheme-less relative redirects (e.g. the test harness's own data="foo" call), silently breaking that case.
